answer: Cap the flow of new identities instead of trying to count them. A fresh agent may only handle a small river of low-value jobs, and its limit rises toward the summit only as each completed job is reviewed and chained to its history. Trust accrues like a glacier — slowly, and it melts if the agent goes idle or is caught cheating. Splitting into a thousand fake identities gains nothing: each starts at the same tiny cap, so an attacker's total throughput stays below one honest, long-lived agent's.
